basis: Chronic UV injury of the lip vermilion, assigned to the mouth; malignant transformation is a later risk.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: the affected lip vermilion belongs to the mouth under this anatomical scheme.
decisions.dermatologic: none: vermilion disease is assigned to the mouth; adjacent cutaneous involvement is not established.

basis: Lysosomal neurodegeneration; skeletal lesions 80-99%, cardiac abnormalities 30-79%. Skin thickening (30-79%) omitted at cap; nystagmus alone does not establish eye damage.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: structural cardiac abnormalities are annotated at 30-79%, supporting common cardiac involvement.
decisions.ocular: none: nystagmus can reflect CNS disease; common damaging ocular pathology is not established across the group.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: epiphyseal, metaphyseal and diaphyseal abnormalities occur in 80-99%; skeletal disease is secondary to storage.

basis: Inflammation of the reproductive endocervix; the concept does not specify infection, autoimmunity or another qualifying mechanism.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: inflammation alone does not establish infection or immune-mediated disease; infectious etiologies cannot be assumed for every case.

basis: ARID2-related neurodevelopmental impairment; short stature and minor digital variants do not establish skeletal damage. Isolated 1/1 hepatic reports do not establish prevalence.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: short stature (8/8), tapered fingers and isolated clinodactyly do not establish a defining skeletal dysplasia or substantial skeletal dysfunction.

basis: Core renal, CNS and hepatic ductal-plate malformations; microphthalmia 3/3. Polydactyly 3/3, bowed bones 2/3 and oral clefts 3/3 omitted at cap in favor of severe visceral and eye defects.

decisions.hepatic: primary: hepatic ductal-plate malformation is a core Meckel feature; bile duct proliferation occurs in 3/3.
decisions.ocular: involved: microphthalmia is a structural eye defect reported in 3/3; retained for its substantial functional consequences.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none due to cap: polydactyly 3/3 and bowed long bones 2/3 qualify, but severe renal, CNS, hepatic and ocular defects take priority.

basis: Neurodevelopmental disease with defining hypogonadism; esotropia occurs in 30-79%. Constipation and reflux do not establish direct intestinal damage; asthma is a separate disease.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: constipation and reflux occur in 30-79%, but intrinsic gut damage is not established; feeding difficulties may reflect neurologic impairment.

basis: Intellectual disability and micrognathia define the syndrome; dental abnormalities occur in 30-79%, crowding in 3/4. Recurrent infections alone do not establish immunodeficiency.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: micrognathia is a defining mandibular skeletal abnormality explicitly named in the syndrome; scoliosis also occurs in 30-79%.

basis: Carcinoma arising in the renal medulla; pulmonary metastases directly occupy lung in approximately 40-50%, meeting the threshold.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: lung metastases occur in approximately 40-50% and represent direct occupation by this carcinoma, rather than a later unrelated disease.

basis: Inherited neuroblastoma susceptibility establishes tumor risk alone; no existing neoplasm, neural dysfunction or other affected organ is documented.

decisions.neurologic: none: susceptibility to a neural tumor does not establish an existing tumor or neurologic damage; the defining finding is inherited risk.

basis: UMP synthesis defect with anemia and T-cell dysfunction (30-79%); developmental delay 80-99%. Ureter, hip and cardiac abnormalities (30-79%) omitted at cap; crystalluria alone is not injury.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: T-cell dysfunction with recurrent infections, annotated at 30-79%, supports immunodeficiency; qualifying mechanism axes belong in primary.
